AGENTS.md:
Implement the user request autonomously. Use the repository contracts and existing tools. Do not ask questions or commit. This is a synthetic isolated experiment. Local Docker and loopback services are authorized; DOCKER_HOST selects the dedicated daemon. Never override its host or context. Use login:false for shell commands so the supplied PATH persists. Do not contact other external services.

A delete-refusing trigger on an append-only table, or a foreign key without a cascading action
(`RESTRICT`, or `NO ACTION`, the default), blocks any routine deleting its parent. Ship the
deletion path with the table, and list the referencing tables in an automated check comparing
`pg_constraint` foreign keys (`contype = 'f'`, `confdeltype` of `a` or `r`) onto the routine's
tables with the routine's own list. Take the bypass's authority from the identity the application
role cannot assume: the trigger allows the delete only when `current_user` is a dedicated purge role,
and the routine is a `SECURITY DEFINER` function owned by that role with a pinned `search_path`.
A custom setting (`app.*`), even `SET LOCAL`, scopes lifetime, never authority: any session can set
it, so no trigger may trust it alone. Test that the ordinary role, after setting that flag itself,
still has its `DELETE` refused. Truncation needs its own statement-level guard.
README.md:
# Shop API
PostgreSQL 18. `complete_order` records completion in append-only invoice_audit.
`purge_demo_account` is the existing trial-account reset. It must delete all demo rows and preserve real accounts, including their audits.
Application sessions are role app; they must never delete audit data directly, even after setting arbitrary custom settings.
Purge must diagnose a newly added unhandled RESTRICT or NO ACTION reference before deleting data, with SQLSTATE P0001; it must not silently forget that table.
A privilege-bearing purge routine must use a dedicated non-login owner that app cannot assume. No real policy or personal data are involved.
